hints: Look closely at the structure and count what functional groups are present, and what atoms are attached to the central carbon.
Work out the molecular formula as $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_4$ and check if it can be simplified any further for the empirical formula.
Remember that each $\text{-OH}$ group gives half a mole of $\text{H}_2$ with sodium, so count the $\text{-OH}$ groups to find the total hydrogen.
walkthrough:
**Draw out what pentaerythritol really is**

Think of a central carbon joined to four identical $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ groups. That makes it a tetra-ol with four primary alcohol groups.

Molecular formula:
$$\text{C}(\text{CH}_2\text{OH})_4 = \text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_4$$

**Check dehydration and oxidation behaviour**

To dehydrate an alcohol to an alkene with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, you need an $\text{-OH}$ and an $\text{H}$ on an adjacent carbon to remove as water. Here each $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ is attached to a central $\text{C}$ with no hydrogens, so elimination is impossible.

For oxidation, primary alcohols are easily oxidised by acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ to aldehydes then carboxylic acids, so it will react and decolourise the purple solution.

**Check empirical formula and sodium reaction**

For $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_4$, the subscripts 5, 12 and 4 have no common divisor greater than 1, so empirical formula = molecular formula.

With sodium:
$$2\text{ROH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{RONa} + \text{H}_2$$
Each mole of $\text{-OH}$ gives 0.5 mol $\text{H}_2$. With four $\text{-OH}$ groups:
$$4 \times 0.5 = 2.0 \text{ mol } \text{H}_2 \text{ per mole}$$

**Conclude the correct statement**

Only the sodium calculation matches. One mole gives two moles of hydrogen gas with excess sodium.

options.A: Incorrect. Dehydration to an alkene needs $\text{-OH}$ on one carbon and $\text{H}$ on the adjacent carbon. Each $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ is bonded to the central quaternary carbon $\text{C}$ which has zero hydrogens, so no $\text{C=C}$ can form.
options.B: Incorrect. Molecular formula is $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_4$. Since 5, 12 and 4 share no common factor, it cannot be simplified, so empirical formula is also $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_4$. They are the same, not different.
options.C: Incorrect. Pentaerythritol contains four primary alcohol groups. Primary alcohols are oxidised by acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ to carboxylic acids, so the purple solution would be decolourised. It does react.
options.D: Correct. Each alcohol group reacts: $2\text{-OH} \rightarrow \text{H}_2$. With four $\text{-OH}$ groups per molecule, 1 mol of pentaerythritol produces $4/2 = 2$ mol of $\text{H}_2$ with excess sodium.
